clue.text: With pioneering ideas beating the clock?

definitions.meaning: someone with ideas too advanced for their era is ahead of their age
playfully, arriving earlier than the clock says one should, ahead of schedule

explanation.surface: Praise for an innovator who also races against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person ahead of their era, and literally reads as being early, which is what beating the clock means.

clue.text: Brag about physician in inflated language

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the boasting word wraps the doctor

parts.note: to brag is to boast
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor boasting in pompous, overblown speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, high-flown speech with little substance.

clue.text: Front liner

parts.note: not a soldier in the trenches but the person standing at the very head of a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A soldier serving on the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: The person at the head of a waiting line is literally the one in front of the line.

clue.text: It isn't steep, pram can make it

indicators.note: the letters of the word pram can make another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentle incline that a pram can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges PRAM; the final 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a gentle slope, a sloping surface that is not steep.

clue.text: In the manor, a chewy vegetable

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Tough greens served at a country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Orache is a leafy plant eaten like spinach, a garden vegetable.

clue.text: London area still in a state of rapture

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London (East Central)
still, not moving, means static

explanation.surface: Someone in a part of London is standing motionless, overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy, carried away by delight.

clue.text: It has been given to one with a change of heart

definitions.text: It has been given to one with a change of heart

parts.words: It has been given to one with a change of heart
parts.note: a change of heart here is literal: a patient receiving a donor heart in surgery

explanation.surface: Someone who has changed their mind gets a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart replacement operation is an organ graft from a donor, which is what the patient receives.

clue.text: Reciprocal contract in which policyholders are shareholders

definitions.text: Reciprocal contract in which policyholders are shareholders

parts.words: Reciprocal contract in which policyholders are shareholders
parts.note: describes a type of cover where members own the company and insure one another

explanation.surface: A description of a cooperative cover arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a scheme is owned by its members, who share profits and insure each other jointly.

clue.text: After inspiration suddenly expire

parts.note: inspiration is breathing in and expire is breathing out, so a sudden blast of breath after a sharp intake

explanation.surface: Someone dies abruptly after a creative idea strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden involuntary expulsion of air following a sharp intake of breath.

clue.text: Doctor taken in by girl on African xylophone

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the girl's name goes around the doctor

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is charmed by a girl playing an African instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The marimba is a wooden-keyed percussion instrument of African origin, like a large xylophone.

clue.text: Stanley accepts equality, being very strict

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the short name holds the word for equality

parts.note: Stan is short for Stanley
par means equality, as in on a par

explanation.surface: A man named Stanley believes in equal treatment and stern rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and rigorously disciplined, like the people of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: It's a foreign wine

parts.note: a plain description of an Italian sparkling wine, with the letters of the opening two words read backwards giving it as a bonus

explanation.surface: Someone identifying an imported wine.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals a reversal, but IT'S A read backwards spells the wine, a playful extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white from Piedmont in Italy, an imported bottle to the setter's readers.

clue.text: Despicable person has low-priced fish

parts.note: low-priced means cheap
a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A villain owns some bargain seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who avoids paying is looked down on as mean and contemptible.

clue.text: Had sent an order in the post that had been cancelled

definitions.text: Had sent an order in the post
definitions.meaning: to have applied for something by letter, mailing away for it
describing a debt or vehicle declared lost or void

explanation.surface: A mail order that was later cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having applied by letter and, as an adjective, scrapped or annulled.

clue.text: In part undrained treeless zone

indicators.note: In part means only some of the letters of the following word are used

explanation.surface: A partly waterlogged, treeless region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast frozen Arctic plain where trees cannot grow.

clue.text: He included, after lunch time, two beginners and Sidney on the slope

indicators.note: included means held inside, so the word he wraps the other pieces

parts.note: lunch time is one o'clock, giving I as the Roman numeral one
L stands for learner, a beginner, so two of them
Sid is short for Sidney

explanation.surface: After lunch a man brings two learners and Sidney up the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: One o'clock as lunch time gives I; L is the learner plate on a British car, so two learners are LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillside is the sloping side of a hill.

clue.text: Handyman, fellow to perform outside with hesitation

indicators.note: outside means the verb for perform goes around the little word to

parts.note: to perform is to act
taken as written
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A handyman hesitantly performing tasks outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a general servant or helper who does all kinds of jobs.

clue.text: Hat, it could have been placed on a Scotsman, an islander

indicators.note: placed on means the first piece sits before the man's name
could have been signals the words hat and it rearranged into another order

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A hat could have been put on a Scot to make him look like an island native.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the South Pacific island of Tahiti is one of its inhabitants.

clue.text: One suitably employed?

parts.note: suitably is read as making suits, so a person whose job is making suits

explanation.surface: A person in a fitting job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes suits, so suit-making is literally the trade.

clue.text: Explosive noises about demand for political union

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters of noises blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Loud bangs around a call for political union.
explanation.definitionFit: Enosis is the movement for union of Cyprus with Greece, a political union campaign.

clue.text: Is it wise, having removed panties?

indicators.note: removed read as re-moved, the letters of panties moved around again

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether taking off underwear is sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise or discerning.

clue.text: Unendingly seek information from a foreign agent

indicators.note: Unendingly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to consult is to seek information

explanation.surface: Someone constantly questions a foreign spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is an official representing their country abroad, a government agent overseas.

clue.text: I name an inquiry that's under consideration

parts.note: an inquiry is a question

explanation.surface: Someone names an investigation that is still being considered.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in doubt or being discussed is one currently under debate.

clue.text: Shed a tear

definitions.meaning: to shed is to let fall, as leaves from a tree
a tear is a single bead of liquid from the eye

explanation.surface: Someone cries over a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fall is the verb; a single bead of liquid is the noun.

clue.text: Neat sum to fine a litter lout?

definitions.text: sum to fine a litter lout?
definitions.meaning: a large amount of money is idiomatically a substantial one, and fining someone for mess suits a word for orderly

explanation.surface: A large penalty for dropping rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means orderly, and a large amount of money is idiomatically a substantial one.

clue.text: Unpack, but have nothing to write while away from home

parts.note: O is the shape of zero, nothing
a pen is something to write with
out means not at home

explanation.surface: Someone unpacks but finds no pen while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold or spread something out, as one does with a parcel.

clue.text: CIC seen developing school subject

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters change into a new form

explanation.surface: A commanding officer seen developing a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Science is a subject taught in classrooms, covering physics, chemistry and biology.

clue.text: It's a job not to be working for someone else

definitions.text: It's a job not to be working for someone else

parts.words: It's a job not to be working for someone else
parts.note: describes work where you are your own boss, with no outside employer

explanation.surface: A remark that it is hard not to work for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Running one's own business means having no employer but oneself.
